reasoning_traces.think:
The core task involves binary classification of match outcomes—specifically, whether a team secures at least one point. This is modeled as a supervised learning problem using engineered features representing squad structure (average age), tactical deployment (formation usage), and key-player exposure (minutes played). The workflow integrates tidyverse for data handling and tidymodels for ML, ensuring reproducibility and interpretability. The small dataset size necessitates careful algorithm selection and validation to avoid overfitting. The empirical approach aligns with business analytics constraints, prioritizing practicality over complexity. Key predictors identified include average team age and key-player minutes, indicating their influence on match performance. The use of global diagnostics ensures transparency in interpretation, mitigating risks from correlated features or missing data. This framework enables decision support for tactical planning and squad management.
